newsitem.title: USA: Value Health, Columbia/HCA $1.2 billion merger delayed.
newsitem.headline: Value Health, Columbia/HCA $1.2 billion merger delayed.

text.p: Value Health Inc. said Friday that a Massachusetts court ruling will delay completion of its planned $1.2 billion merger with Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp.

The court granted a preliminary injunction at the request of FHC Options Inc., which said its partnership with a Value Health subsidiary to provide mental health services to Medicaid beneficiaries would have been hurt by the merger.

Value Health said the partnership has submitted a revised plan to Massachusetts officials to eliminate any conflict of interest and is in talks with the state's medical assistance division about the plan.

"We anticipate the transaction will close as soon as the preliminary injunction granted today is lifted and certain regulatory matters concerning the State of California Department of Corporations are resolved," Value Health said in a statement late on Friday.
Columbia/HCA also said the merger would close as soon as the injunction is lifted and as soon as California regulatory issues were resolved.
Neither company gave details on the regulatory issues in California and phone calls to both companies were not immediately returned.
Value Health said in its release that it expects to return to court early next week with new information.
The companies in January said they would merge in a stock swap valued at $1.3 billion and in April revised the terms and the price to $1.2 billion.
The deal, which was approved Value Health shareholders last week, was scheduled to be completed in the second quarter.
Value Health stock fell 62.5 cents to $19.50 while Columbia/HCA rose 62.5 cents to $39.50, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
